text:
Ravi: rolling out kestrel-lite-ptq to dedicated-canary. quick smoke shows ~0.9% structured-output parse failures on funcall stream. odd pattern: truncated array tails and sometimes a leading BOM (﻿) in the middle of the payload. sample from live canary replay:

````
{"action": "rank", "args": {"items": ["doc1", "doc2", "doc3"
﻿
````

Nora: BOM in the middle?? that smells like encoding handling when streaming chunks are stitched. did you bisect runtime vs proxy?

Ravi: initial bisect points to runtime kernel edge-case in the int8 path. switching to non-streaming removes BOM but raises median latency by ~45ms.

Sam: iirc we saw a similar symptom with older PTQ where partial multibyte UTF-8 sequences across chunk boundaries produced stray replacement chars. BOM is stranger though. can you dump raw bytes around boundary?

Ravi: posted hex dump to the canary bucket. looks like a 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF sequence appears immediately after a flush boundary. not present in fp16 baseline.

Liu: proposal: 1) add server-side interstitial sanitizer that strips Unicode BOMs and control-range bytes before parse. 2) emit telemetry: funcall_parse.fail.raw, .fail.sanitized, .heal.attempt, .heal.success. 3) implement a streaming sentinel that ensures arrays/objects are closed before the final chunk is published (best-effort).

Nora: +1 on metrics. also suggest a conservative client-side backoff tweak: if parse fails and a healer modifies payload, don't auto-retry the tool call — instead surface healed response with an indicator so callers can dedupe. duplicates are inflating downstream billing.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy kestrel-lite-ptq -> started (2025-02-14T16:11Z)

Sam: we should add a tiny parser-heal library inside runtime: heuristics order: 1) strip leading/trailing BOM/control bytes, 2) remove trailing partial-utf8 bytes, 3) try appending common closers ("]", "}"), 4) if still invalid, do conservative truncation up to last valid JSON token and mark as truncated. log both original + healed payload with model tag. Flaggable per-model.

Ravi: i'll sketch the PR. want to keep sanitizer very height-limited to avoid masking real model regressions. add unit tests with multi-chunk streaming and fuzzed boundary bytes.

Liu: schedule a replay eval: run 5k canary samples through strict schema-lint and also through healer-on and healer-off branches. capture heal rate, duplicate-tool-invokes, and end-to-end tail latency delta. add a dashboard with those three panels.

Nora: also run a benchmark compare (fp16 vs int8) for token-emission boundaries to validate kernel patch doesn't regress throughput. if healer hides a bigger issue we need that signal.

Ravi: PR will include opt-in config + kill-switch and opt-out per model. pinging @Sam for review. :eyes:

Sam: will review. also start a grep across last 14 days for similar hex patterns across other canaries; if >3 models impacted we flip the default to on with a 2-week watch.

Ravi: sounds good. i'll post the grep results here once done.

Liu: thanks all — i'll create the replay job and link the dashboard when queued.
